chunks: As for what was narrated by Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr, from Udaym ibn al-Ḥurr, who said:

I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: Indeed, Jabrāʾīl عليه السلام instructed the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم regarding all the salats, and he assigned for every salat two times, except al-maghrib, for he assigned to it one single time.

key_terms.جَبْرَئِيلَ: Jibril, the angel who conveyed divine instruction
key_terms.رَسُولَ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.وَقْتَيْنِ: two prayer times or two valid periods for performance

ai.seo_question: Does every daily salat have two times, and is salat al-maghrib an exception?
ai.summary: This hadith states that Jabrāʾīl عليه السلام taught the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم the prescribed times of the daily salats. It indicates that each salat has two time periods, except salat al-maghrib, which has one designated time.
